application.cv_markdown:
MARCO NOVAK

marco.novak@mail.example | +358 00 000 0180

CAREER HISTORY

Tuulenkaari Satellite Systems | Signal Processing Engineer | Oulu | 2012 - present

- Implemented the matched filter and pulse compression chain in C++ for the RSat-4 synthetic aperture radar processor, targeting the TI C66x DSP platform with hard real-time constraints
- Built and maintained the mission data processing pipeline in Python (3.8+), including automated orbit-correlated range corrections and batch image formation, running on the operations centre's Linux cluster
- Served as the sole English-language interface with EORA's Concurrent Design Facility during the Phase-A study for the ArcticWatch mission, preparing all technical documentation in English
- Based in Oulu since joining Tuulenkaari in 2012; relocated from Japan after graduation

Career gap: 2014-2015 -- made redundant during Tuulenkaari's restructuring; completed Suvanto's satellite systems engineering certification programme during this period

SELECTED PROJECTS

RSat-4 Ground Segment Development (2017-2019)
- Conducted S-band antenna pattern measurements and RF chain calibration for the ground segment receive equipment using a Rohde & Schwarz ZVL network analyser
- Applied electromagnetic field theory and Fourier transform methods from electrical engineering coursework at the Sakura National University to diagnose a persistent sidelobe artefact in the ground station antenna
- Integrated the RSat-4 payload data handling chain for a 500 km sun-synchronous orbit, including onboard data compression verification and downlink budget validation

ArcticWatch Feasibility Study (2020-2021)
- Participated as an EU citizen (Czech nationality) in this EORA-funded study, which required EU/EEA work authorisation for access to restricted documentation

EDUCATION

Sakura National University -- MEng Electrical Engineering, 2011

TECHNICAL SKILLS

- Phased-array signal processing: designed scan-angle-dependent calibration weights for Tuulenkaari's 32-element L-band receive array, achieving <0.3 dB gain variation across +/-45 degree scan
- DSP: SAR image formation, pulse compression, matched filtering
- Programming: C++ (embedded/real-time), Python (NumPy/SciPy, production pipelines)
- Tools: MATLAB, Simulink, GNU Radio, Git
application.cover_letter_markdown:
In 2019, I delivered the ground segment for the RSat-4 mission three weeks ahead of schedule and with no open non-conformance reports at final review. I mention this not because on-time delivery should be noteworthy, but because in satellite programmes it genuinely is, and it was the result of disciplined systems work that I have been building for most of my career.

I have been with Tuulenkaari Satellite Systems in Oulu since 2012, when I moved here from Tokyo after completing my engineering degree at the Sakura National University. Starting at a small Finnish satellite company as a graduate from a Japanese university was an unusual path, but it gave me early ownership of problems that a larger organisation would have divided among several teams. Over fourteen years I have worked on embedded C++ firmware for SAR processors, built the Python data pipeline that handles our mission data from downlink through to processed imagery, and conducted hands-on RF measurements on ground station equipment.

My career was interrupted in 2014 when Tuulenkaari restructured and my position was eliminated. I used the following year to complete a certification programme in satellite systems engineering at Suvanto, which turned out to be one of the most valuable professional experiences I have had. It forced me to understand the full mission lifecycle rather than only the signal processing layer, and when Tuulenkaari brought me back in late 2015, I returned with a much wider perspective on how the pieces fit together.

I am interested in Kaikuvaara because your instrument work sits at the boundary between antenna engineering and signal processing, which is the intersection where I have done my best technical work. The RSat-4 ground station project is the clearest example: I calibrated the RF receive chain, diagnosed antenna pattern artefacts using electromagnetic theory from my university training, and made the complete system work as an integrated unit. I am most effective when the work requires someone who thinks across subsystem boundaries.

What appeals to me about this role specifically is that Kaikuvaara seems to value engineers who work across the full stack, from algorithm through to hardware. That is how I have always operated -- my embedded DSP work means I understand the hardware constraints that shape what algorithms can realistically do, and my pipeline work means I can handle the data processing chain end to end. I am most useful when the problem involves real constraints rather than simulation alone.

On the practical side: I am a Czech citizen with full EU work authorisation and have been based in Oulu for fourteen years. All my professional work is conducted in English. I am not looking to relocate and would welcome the opportunity to continue working in this city.

I understand that Kaikuvaara's instruments involve domains I have not encountered in my radar work. But the core discipline -- making signal processing work reliably on hardware that must function without intervention in harsh environments -- is the same problem I have spent fourteen years getting better at.

I am available for an interview at your convenience.

Marco Novak

extraction_contract.task: You are the extraction step of a candidate-screening support tool. For the one candidate in this task, read the CV and cover letter in full and classify, for EACH of the 12 requirements listed, exactly one status from this fixed vocabulary: evidence_found, claim_only, contradiction, not_stated. This is extraction, not evaluation -- you are locating and quoting what the text says, never judging whether the candidate is good enough.

status_definitions.evidence_found: The text gives a concrete, specific example of the requirement (a named project, employer, tool, or role detail) -- not just a keyword or a bare assertion.
status_definitions.claim_only: The requirement is asserted (e.g. listed as a skill, or claimed in a sentence) but with no concrete project, employer, or detail backing it up.
status_definitions.contradiction: Two statements in the application -- CV vs CV, letter vs letter, or CV vs letter -- cannot both be true at once about this requirement (e.g. a degree conferral date that is later than a job that required the degree; a claimed leadership title alongside a work-history entry that describes an individual-contributor role for the same employer and period). Quote both conflicting statements. Do not decide which statement is correct or resolve the conflict -- record that it exists.
status_definitions.not_stated: The text does not explicitly and unambiguously address the requirement, under any name for it, canonical or otherwise.

extraction_contract.refuse_to_guess_rule: REFUSE TO GUESS. If the requirement is not explicitly and unambiguously addressed in the text, the status is not_stated -- full stop. Never infer a requirement from a related or similar-sounding skill, a job title alone, general seniority, years of experience, or the prestige of an employer or university. A candidate whose job title was 'Senior RF Engineer' has NOT thereby evidenced hands-on RF measurement work unless the text itself describes that work. Where the text describes substantive work in different words from the requirement's own name, quote what the text actually says and let the quoted substance speak; what a description in adjacent vocabulary amounts to is a judgement call for the human recruiter, not something this extraction step resolves by guessing in either direction. When genuinely unsure between two statuses, choose the more conservative one (not_stated over claim_only, claim_only over evidence_found) and say so in the line's note.
extraction_contract.no_verdict_rule: This tool never ranks, scores, shortlists, rejects, or recommends a candidate, and never characterises the candidate as a whole. Do not use words or phrases like recommend, reject, shortlist, rank, top candidate, best, worst, strong candidate, weak candidate, good fit, poor fit, hire, do not hire, suitable, unsuitable, pass, advance, or any other language that compares this candidate to others or states what should happen to their application. State only what the text shows, per requirement. The recruiter decides; this output is preparation, not a decision.
extraction_contract.citation_rule: Every evidence_found, claim_only, or contradiction line must carry a VERBATIM quote: copied character-for-character from the CV or cover letter text given to you (leading/trailing whitespace may be trimmed, but do not paraphrase, summarise, correct, translate, or combine separate sentences). Tag every quote with its source: 'cv' or 'cover_letter'. A quote that cannot be found verbatim in the source document will fail citation verification and be reported as invented evidence -- when in doubt, quote a shorter, exact fragment rather than a paraphrase.
extraction_contract.ask_in_screening_rule: For EVERY must-have requirement (category 'must_have') whose status you set to not_stated, add one entry to the top-level ask_in_screening list: a plain, neutral, single-sentence question the recruiter could ask in a screening call to find out. Do not add ask_in_screening entries for desirable or constraint requirements, and do not add one for a must-have that is not not_stated. Questions must be neutral fact-finding, never leading and never implying a verdict (e.g. 'Can you describe your hands-on RF measurement experience, if any?' -- not 'Do you actually have RF experience, since your CV doesn't show it?').

return_format.description: Return a single JSON object for this one candidate (when extraction runs in a batch of 8, return a JSON array of 8 such objects, one per candidate, in the same order as the batch's `tasks` list).

schema.candidate_id: string, must match the task's candidate_id

requirements.status: one of: evidence_found, claim_only, contradiction, not_stated

lines.quote: verbatim quote from the application text (see citation_rule)

requirements.note: string or null -- required and must explain the conflict without resolving it when status is 'contradiction'; optional free-text otherwise (e.g. to flag a conservative-status judgement call under refuse_to_guess_rule)

return_format.note: The `requirements` array must contain exactly one entry per requirement given in this task, in the same order, covering all 12 requirement ids.
